query: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloys are promising bond-coat candidates because of their mechanical properties and elevated-temperature oxidation resistance. Earlier HVAF-M3 work identified 15–45 μm feedstock as optimal for high-quality coatings, but applying the same composition and size range with the HVAF-i7 torch yielded acceptable coating quality yet inadequate thickness. Separate studies of conventional MCrAlY bond coats using the M3 system reported a slight gain in deposition efficiency at higher particle velocity and nozzle-specific best spray distances of 300 and 350 mm. The design target is a sufficiently thick, adherent bond coat that retains coating integrity, minimal as-sprayed oxidation, and durability during high-temperature thermal-barrier service, including deposition within internal diameters as small as 120 mm. What single intervention could overcome the thickness limitation? State the hypothesized intervention and mechanism, predict the outcome relative to the 15–45 μm-feedstock baseline, define the deposition and service conditions under which it should remain effective, identify supporting evidence from the cited prior studies, and propose a controlled experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Increasing the particle velocity and using a nozzle-to-substrate distance of 300–350 mm during HVAF‐i7 spraying will improve deposition efficiency and result in a thicker, adherent FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy bond coat with minimal as-sprayed oxidation.
generation.material_initial_state: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy powder with a feedstock size of 15–45 μm (gas-atomized) as currently used in HVAF deposition.
generation.intervention: Adjust the HVAF-i7 processing parameters by increasing the in-flight particle velocity and setting the nozzle-to-substrate distance to the optimized range of 300–350 mm.
generation.conditions: Deposition is performed using the HVAF-i7 torch, including on substrates with internal diameters as small as 120 mm; the bond coats must later withstand high-temperature thermal-barrier service (in the range up to ~1100 °C) with minimal oxidation.
generation.structural_mediator: Enhanced particle kinetic energy improves the deformation and the inter-splat bonding on impact, leading to better material retention and thicker deposits, while the optimized spray distance minimizes excessive in-flight oxidation.
generation.mechanism: By increasing the particle velocity, the momentum upon impact is higher, which enables particles to flatten and bond more effectively to the substrate. The nozzle distance of 300–350 mm provides a balance that minimizes undesirable oxidation yet delivers sufficient heat for metallurgical bonding. Together, these adjustments overcome the thickness limitations observed with the baseline HVAF-i7 process.
generation.predicted_outcome: Under the enhanced parameter setting, the produced coating will be measurably thicker (improved deposition efficiency) compared to the baseline process using the same 15–45 μm powder, while maintaining adherence, microstructural integrity, and controlled oxidation similar to that seen in MCrAlY coatings.
generation.baseline: The existing 15–45 μm feedstock deposited via HVAF-M3 (or HVAF-i7 with previous parameters) that yields acceptable coating quality but inadequate thickness.
generation.boundary: This intervention is expected to be effective in HVAF-i7 systems applied to both flat surfaces and restricted geometries (e.g., internal diameters of 120 mm) and in service environments where the bond coat will be exposed to high temperatures (up to ~1100 °C).
generation.uncertainty: The precise increase in coating thickness and the balance between improved deposition and oxidation control are uncertain and may depend on fine-tuning the particle velocity and exact nozzle distance. There is also some uncertainty about the transferability of the MCrAlY optimized parameters to high-entropy alloys.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform a controlled study depositing FeCoNiCrAl bond coats using HVAF-i7 on substrates with 120 mm internal diameters. Two groups are compared: one using the baseline HVAF-i7 parameters and the other using the increased particle velocity with a nozzle-to-substrate distance of 300–350 mm. All other parameters (e.g., powder size, composition, and substrate pre-treatment) should be held constant.
measurements: Coating thickness (via cross-sectional SEM or profilometry)
Adhesion strength (using pull-off or scratch tests)
Oxidation level and phase composition (using XRD and EDS analysis)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The intervention hypothesis will be falsified if the coatings produced under the increased particle velocity and optimized nozzle distance do not show a statistically significant increase in thickness while maintaining or improving adhesion and oxidation resistance relative to the baseline.

cited_evidence.text: As reported in [,,,], HVOF as-sprayed AlTiCrFeCoNi coatings possessed a dense microstructure and a high microhardness over 750 HV with a good fracture toughness. The heat-treated NiCoFeCrSiAlTi coating exhibits a hardness even higher than 800 HV, good wear resistance, and oxidation resistance at 1100 °C, similar to that of MCrAlY coating []. The cavitation erosion resistance of the AlCoCrFeNi coating is about 3.5 times that of 06Cr13Ni5Mo steel in the same environment []. The high wear resistance of AlCoCrFeNi-based HEA at elevated temperatures is associated with oxidation behavior. The formation of a compact oxide layer on the AlCoCrFeNi and AlTiCrFeCoNi HVOF coatings accounts for enhanced wear resistance at temperatures ≥ 800 °C [] and a lowered coefficient of friction due to its function as a solid lubricant []. In [], it was found that additions of Nd and Mo to a AlCrFeCoNi base significantly reduced the wear depth at increasing temperatures due to improved oxide layer adhesion. Thus, AlCoCrFeNiMo coatings deposited using HVOF are suitable for high-temperature application. A unique feature of thermal spray processes is the extremely high heating and cooling rates (>106 K/s) [,,

AlCoCrFeNi alloys can be used as protective coatings for the thermal parts of aero-engines, which gives them broad application prospects. Researchers have made a relatively systematic study of the AlCoCrFeNi alloy, but there are few studies of the AlCoCrFeNi coating, and the research into the high temperature oxidation and phase transformation of AlCoCrFeNi coatings is not comprehensive enough. This work, therefore, focuses on this aspect. The AlCoCrFeNi coatings were prepared by atmospheric plasma spraying (APS) and oxidized isothermally at 650–1000 °C in order to study their oxidation behavior [,,,]. The formation and evolution process of oxides were determined, and the phase transition of the coating interior was investigated to find out the oxidation mechanism.

reading.lever: Increase particle velocity and adjust nozzle-to-substrate distance (300–350 mm) during HVAF-i7 spraying.
reading.why: This parameter adjustment, validated in MCrAlY studies, is likely to enhance deposition efficiency and overcome the coating thickness limitation.
